difference.definition: per-fold paired difference (this configuration minus the candidate), mean plus or minus one standard error

one_se.source: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman (2009), The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., §7.10 (the one-standard-error rule)
one_se.text: The one-standard-error rule keeps the simplest configuration whose mean is within one standard error of the best one.

texts.en: The one-standard-error rule keeps the simplest configuration whose mean is within one standard error of the best one.
texts.fr: La règle d'une erreur type retient la configuration la plus simple dont la moyenne est à moins d'une erreur type de la meilleure.

one_se.simplicity: the linear family first, then fewer features, then a stronger penalty; a tie keeps the candidate

optimism.method: mean over folds of (the fold's best configuration minus the configuration best on the mean), in the direction of the metric
optimism.source: Tibshirani & Tibshirani (2009), A bias correction for the minimum error rate in cross-validation, Annals of Applied Statistics 3(2): 822-829
optimism.text: Choosing the best of several configurations on the same folds flatters it: the optimism is the average gap, fold by fold, between that fold's best configuration and the one chosen.

texts.en: Choosing the best of several configurations on the same folds flatters it: the optimism is the average gap, fold by fold, between that fold's best configuration and the one chosen.
texts.fr: Choisir la meilleure de plusieurs configurations sur les mêmes plis la flatte : l'optimisme est l'écart moyen, pli par pli, entre la meilleure configuration du pli et celle retenue.

optimism.note: Approximate: an estimate of how much the best mean owes to having chosen it among these configurations.

advice.text: At least one variant differs from the candidate by more than the noise between folds. Another variant is possible within the budget, each one counted.

texts.en: At least one variant differs from the candidate by more than the noise between folds. Another variant is possible within the budget, each one counted.
texts.fr: Au moins une variante diffère du candidat de plus que le bruit entre les plis. Une autre variante reste possible dans le budget, chacune comptée.

model_selection.note: Development evidence: every configuration is compared on the same out-of-fold predictions of the development rows. The fold standard errors ignore the overlap of the folds' training rows (Bengio & Grandvalet 2004), so they understate the noise: the advice errs towards stopping late, not early. The final test, opened once, is not affected by this choice.

smearing.note: The model predicts the target on its own scale (no transform of the target), so no retransformation correction such as Duan's smearing applies. Smearing is not implemented: a log-transformed target would need it.

values.normality_note: The quantile-quantile points compare the standardised residuals with a normal distribution. Normality is not needed for the mean error or the coefficients with this many rows (Lumley et al. 2002); it matters for prediction intervals, which this study does not give.

qq.definition: Quantiles of the residuals standardised by their mean and standard deviation, against the same quantiles of a normal distribution: on a straight diagonal line when the residuals are normal.

by_prediction.binning: 10 equal-count bins of the prediction, in prediction order

heteroscedasticity.rule: Flagged when the rank correlation of the absolute residual with the prediction is at least 0.2 in size, or the residual standard deviation of the top third of the predictions is more than 1.5 times (or less than 1/1.5 of) that of the bottom third
heteroscedasticity.meaning: An error that grows with the prediction makes one interval width wrong for every row; the mean error stays a fair summary.

coefficients.note: Coefficients of the model fitted on these rows, with Wald intervals from a robust (sandwich) standard error: the approximation of how much each coefficient would move if the rows were drawn again, the preparation of the variables kept as fitted. Associations given the other variables, never effects. The fit is penalised: its coefficients are pulled towards zero, so the intervals describe the spread of the penalised estimate, centred on a value that is itself shrunk; they are not exact confidence intervals of an unpenalised coefficient, and a coefficient of a rare category can be shrunk well inside its interval.
coefficients.scale: target units per standard deviation of the development rows (numeric) or per category (one-hot, not identifiable one by one); associations, not effects

tuning.method: nested cross-validation: within each outer fold, an inner 3-fold cross-validation of the outer training rows picks the value; the model is refitted with it on those rows
tuning.tie: the simplest value of the grid (listed first)
tuning.meaning: ridge penalty strength on the standardised features
tuning.note: The value is chosen inside each outer fold by an inner cross-validation of that fold's training rows only, so the out-of-fold figures include the choice (nested cross-validation). One tuning is one trial.

qq.definition: Quantiles of the residuals standardised by their mean and standard deviation, against the same quantiles of a normal distribution: on a straight diagonal line when the residuals are normal.

heteroscedasticity.meaning: An error that grows with the prediction makes one interval width wrong for every row; the mean error stays a fair summary.

calibration_slope.definition: least-squares slope of the target on the prediction: 1 when the predictions are as spread as the target

linear_checks.method: binned out-of-fold gaps per numeric feature (chi-square, Bonferroni); calibration slope by segment (Cochran's Q); overall calibration slope (Cox 1958)
linear_checks.note: Checks of the candidate linear model on its out-of-fold predictions: a flag is evidence that another model family might follow the data more closely, not proof; choosing a family after seeing it makes that comparison data-contingent.
